newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks shake off weariness to end higher.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks shake off weariness to end higher.

text.p: Swiss shares shook off early weariness to close above important resistance levels of 3,700 and 3,710 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI).
Dealers said the SMI future, which showed a marked rise in the afternoon, was the main reason for the market's good performance, but some window dressing and short covering may also have helped.
The market may be about to leave its recent sideways movement, a trader said, adding the 3,800 level may be within reach if 3,750 points could be overcome.
The SMI added 1.08 percent, or 39.8 points, to 3,736.4 and the all-share SPI was up 20.27 points to 2,393.34.
The October SMI future was up 37 points to 3,737.0.
One dealer warned the situation remained shaky.
"If Wall Street ends 20 points lower, things will go down the drain again", he said. Volumes were overall moderate .
Pharmaceuticals, chemicals and some export-oriented firms posted sizeable gains. Roche added 105 francs 9,235 and Nestle ended 1.6 percent higher at 1,398.
Sulzer jumped 2.5 percent to 737 francs. The shares may see more interest as a technical rise seems to be imminent, a dealer said.
Among financials, UBS overcome technical resistance to end 12 francs higher 1,207.

Building controls and power group Elektrowatt ended two francs lower at 493. There was some disappointment with figures for 1995/96 and the fact that the company did not say anything new about a possible sale of CS Holding's 44.9 percent stake at today's news conference.
Elektrowatt said group net profit for the 1995/96 fiscal year, which ends today, would fall to around 90 million francs from 210 million francs due to provisions.
